chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave and he fathered children with her. He (the Imam) said: 'I have more right to them than you, if you marry.' Then he said: 'The slave does not have the right to take the children from her, and if she marries until he is freed, she has more right to the children than he does, as long as he is a slave. But when he is freed, he has more right to them than she does.'
ai.seo_question: Who has custody of children born to a free woman and a slave slave?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahar, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'al-abu ahaqq bi al-walad' (the father has greater right to the child) by linking paternal custody rights to the father's social status. It establishes that while the mother retains priority during the father's enslavement due to her free status, this right transfers to the father upon his manumission, reflecting the historical legal context where the father's ability to provide and maintain the family unit was tied to his freedom and social standing.
